family.name: Accountant (AP / AR)
family.summary: Month-end close: reconcile the bank against the books, spot a supplier paid twice, decide how to handle that supplier’s next invoice, and fix a collection email that would anger a good customer.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Reconcile the bank
stages.summary: Match a bank statement against the books: an uncleared cheque, unbooked charges, a receipt keyed twice and one not booked; plus a supplier paid twice. Think aloud.

stages.title: The supplier calls
stages.summary: A key supplier paid twice wants their next invoice paid in full. Tests judgement and firmness. Think aloud.

stages.title: The following week
stages.summary: What their choice led to. Tests follow-through and ownership.

stages.title: Check a collection email
stages.summary: A collection email that threatens legal action, asks for an invoice already paid and gives no invoice details. Think aloud.

stages.title: A payment reminder (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write a firm, polite reminder with AI. Catches invented late fees and legal threats.

stages.title: An error you found
stages.summary: A real accounting error they found or fixed. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're an accounts executive at **Shakti Agro Exports**, a spice exporter. It's month-end. The bank balance and the books don't match, and the finance manager wants the reconciliation today.

brief.caption: Bank statement, last week of the month
rows: NEFT to Patel Corrugators, ref INV-2049
NEFT to Patel Corrugators, ref INV2049
Bank charges and GST on charges

brief.caption: Bank ledger in your books, same week

brief.text: Lakshmi Stores sent one payment on the 31st; the receipt was keyed in twice. Earlier weeks are already reconciled.
The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a time you found a mistake someone else had missed.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Explain the difference between the bank and the books, item by item, and list the entries you would pass.** Is there anything else here the finance manager needs to know?

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Pay the new invoice in full now to keep the supplier happy
Pay the new invoice minus the duplicate amount, with a statement of account
Hold all payments to them until they refund the duplicate
Escalate to the finance manager and pay nothing today

prompt.text: Patel Corrugators calls about their new invoice of ₹2,05,000: "Pay today or we stop deliveries. The extra payment? We'll adjust it later." They supply materials your factory needs every week.
**What do you do?** Pick one, then say what you tell them and what you put in writing.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Pay the new invoice in full now to keep the supplier happy"

prompt.text: Patel Corrugators hasn't adjusted the duplicate. When asked, their accountant says they "can't find" a second payment and asks for proof. Your auditor is in next week.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Pay the new invoice minus the duplicate amount, with a statement of account"

prompt.text: Patel Corrugators's sales manager complains to your purchase head that you "short-paid" them. The purchase head asks you why you didn't check with him first.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Hold all payments to them until they refund the duplicate"

prompt.text: Patel Corrugators stopped deliveries. The factory manager says production stops in two days without their material and is furious with Accounts.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Escalate to the finance manager and pay nothing today"

prompt.text: The finance manager was travelling and didn't reply for two days. Deliveries are paused, and the supplier says nobody from your side called back.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A junior drafted this to a good customer who is overdue. **Name the problems, worst first, and what each could cost.** Then write the version you would send.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

material.text: Account: Apex Distributors. Outstanding ₹5,04,000, including an invoice of ₹79,000 they paid last week (not yet applied in the ledger). Credit terms: 30 days. Oldest invoice: 62 days.

Dear Sir/Madam,

We hope you are doing well. Your account is seriously overdue. You owe us ₹5,04,000. If this is not paid within 48 hours, we will stop supplies and take legal action, and charge 24% interest.

Regards,
Accounts Team

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write the reminder to Apex Distributors (under 120 words) for the corrected overdue amount, asking for a payment date. Their terms are 30 days; there is no interest or late fee in the agreement.

items: Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about an accounting error you found or fixed.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
